data.title: Command and Control Over Web Protocols Undetected
data.summary:
A command and control channel operating over HTTPS to an attacker-controlled host
persisted for the duration of the engagement without detection or interruption.
data.description:
Web protocols are the default control channel because they are universally permitted and
because the traffic is encrypted by default, so content inspection is unavailable without
deliberate interception.

What remains observable is behaviour: regular beaconing intervals, consistent request
sizes, long-lived sessions to a destination with no browsing history, and a user agent
that no installed browser produces. Detecting it requires that outbound web traffic be
logged per host and analysed, which is the step most commonly missing.

Destination reputation alone is insufficient. Infrastructure registered for a single
engagement has no reputation to be bad, and categorisation services default to permitting
the unknown.
data.recommendation:
* Log outbound web requests per host at the proxy, including destinations that are allowed,
  and retain them long enough to investigate.
* Alert on beaconing characteristics — interval regularity and request size consistency —
  rather than relying on destination reputation.
* Treat newly registered and uncategorised domains as higher risk by default.
* Break and inspect TLS where lawful and proportionate, acknowledging what cannot be
  inspected.
data.short_recommendation: Log outbound web traffic per host and alert on beaconing behaviour.
